World Club Challenge: Wakefield to take on Sydney Roosters at Headingley on February 19 in England vs Australia clash
Wakefield Trinity to make World Club Challenge debut after winning Super League Grand Final just three years after relegation to the Championship; opponents Sydney Roosters boast a record five wins in this match, level with Wigan Warriors; English clubs victorious in last three games
Saturday 28 November 2026 09:55, UK
Super League champions Wakefield Trinity will face Sydney Roosters in the World Club Challenge at Headingley on February 19.
A maiden appearance in the match between the winners of Super League and the NRL is Wakefield's reward for an astonishing season, which culminated in their 23-10 Grand Final victory over Warrington Wolves at Old Trafford in October, just three years after relegation to the Championship.
Trinity will be looking to make it four straight wins for English clubs in this contest.

St Helens pipped Penrith in 2023 before Wigan and Hull KR recorded wins over Penrith and Brisbane Broncos respectively in 2024 and 2026.
Wakefield owner Matt Ellis said: "The World Club Challenge is the most prestigious game in club rugby league and to be playing the most successful side in the fixture's history is an honour.
"This is the biggest night in Wakefield Trinity's history and it would be fantastic to see our supporters pack out Headingley and make the atmosphere spectacular."
Roosters CEO: This match holds special place in our history
Sydney Roosters boast a joint-record five World Club Challenge titles, matching Wigan's tally, and have never lost the match.
Roosters went back-to-back in 2019 and 2020, beating Wigan for the first of those triumphs and St Helens for the second.
Those successes came amid a run of seven wins in eight years for Australian sides, prior to Covid-19 postponing fixtures and then this current English monopoly.
Sydney Roosters CEO Joe Kelly, whose team won the inaugural edition in 1976, said: "The World Club Challenge holds a special place in the history of the Sydney Roosters, and we are incredibly proud of our record in this prestigious fixture.
"To return to England as reigning NRL Premiers with the opportunity to become six-time World Club champions is an exciting prospect for our entire club."
Wakefield said venues such as Leeds United's Elland Road and Barnsley's Oakwell were also considered to stage the game.
Headingley will host the match for a fourth time, with Leeds Rhinos having taken on Manly, Melbourne and North Queensland in previous editions.
